lesson.picture: An airport. public/index.php is the front door. The kernel is security + check-in (global middleware). Service providers are the ground crew who set everything up before the first flight. The router is the departure board sending you to the right gate (controller).
lesson.concept:
1) public/index.php loads Composer autoload and bootstraps the app (container). 2) The HTTP kernel runs bootstrappers: env, config, exceptions, facades, then registers and boots all service providers — this is where bindings, event listeners, routes are set up. 3) The request passes through global middleware, then the router matches a route, runs route/group middleware (auth, throttle). 4) The controller is resolved from the container (constructor + method injection). 5) The response bubbles back through middleware in reverse and is sent. 6) Terminable middleware runs after the response.

Service providers: register() = only bind things into the container; boot() = safe to use other services (routes, policies, listeners, preventLazyLoading).
lesson.bn: index.php → app bootstrap → HTTP kernel → service provider register/boot → global middleware → router → route middleware → controller (container থেকে DI) → response উল্টো পথে middleware দিয়ে ফেরত। register()-এ শুধু bind, boot()-এ অন্য service ব্যবহার করা যায়।

practice.task: A colleague puts Route::model bindings and an event listener registration inside register() of a provider and it breaks intermittently. Why, and where should it go?
practice.solution:
```php
register() runs before all providers are registered, so the router/event dispatcher it depends on may not be bound yet. Anything that USES other services belongs in boot(), which runs after every provider's register().
```

practice.task: Order these for a request to GET /orders/5 with auth middleware: controller method, global middleware, route middleware, kernel bootstrap, providers boot, response back through middleware.
practice.solution:
```php
kernel bootstrap → providers boot → global middleware → (router matches) → route middleware (auth) → controller method → response back through middleware in reverse → terminable middleware after send.
```

practice.task: Write a middleware that rejects requests without header X-Tenant and stores the tenant on the request. Where do you register it for API routes only?

cards.q: Order: middleware, router, service providers, kernel, index.php
cards.a: index.php → kernel bootstrap → service providers (register then boot) → global middleware → router → route middleware → controller → response back through middleware.

cards.q: register() vs boot() in a service provider
cards.a: register(): only bind into the container, don't use other services (they may not exist yet). boot(): all providers are registered, safe to use anything.

cards.q: How does the controller get its constructor dependencies?
cards.a: The container reflects the constructor's type-hints, resolves each (via bindings or auto-wiring), and builds the controller.

cards.q: Global vs route middleware — give an example of each
cards.a: Global: TrimStrings, HandleCors — runs on every request. Route: auth, throttle, verified — attached to routes/groups.
Middleware with terminate() that runs after the response is sent — e.g. session save, logging — so the user isn't kept waiting.
